external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise's own identity provider that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies group membership changes to the identity broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, consumes HR group membership changes, and writes audit events.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses the token's groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: The key store that holds the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their groups.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: The log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what that log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token is good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: take token
data_flows.description: The store admin console takes the identity broker's token and uses its groups for authorization.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.notes: Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: The public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: keep signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps the signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: keep colleagues and groups
data_flows.description: The identity broker stores colleagues and their group memberships in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The overnight pull is also how leavers stop being colleagues.
data_flows.data_description: Group membership changes, including changes for leavers

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: change prices and void transactions
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console to change prices and void transactions when authorized by the token's store-manager group.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions
data_flows.notes: A store-manager token works against every store.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home
trust_boundaries.description: The home environment from which colleagues may sign in using their own devices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: identity provider
trust_boundaries.description: The boundary controlled by the franchise's own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source names it as a console; the extraction rules define a console as a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The key store holds confidential data because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key; signing keys are secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The directory holds confidential data because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory holds colleagues and the groups they are in; this identifies or describes people.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log holds confidential data because it records sign-ins associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log; sign-in records describe identifiable colleagues.
